Responsible AI & Clinical Safety Framework

About MedClass AI & Safety Ethics

Transparent guidelines on intended use, non-diagnostic boundaries, uncertainty disclosure, and user safety safeguards.

Experiencing an Acute Emergency?

Do not use this application for emergency medical needs. Call your local emergency hotline immediately:

India Emergency: 112Ambulance Service: 108

What the System DOES

  • Classifies the Question: Identifies whether a written question is clinical or non-clinical in nature.
  • Taxonomy Routing: Categorizes inquiry topics into 13 medical specialties (e.g. Cardiology, Endocrinology).
  • Intention Extraction: Detects user intent (Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention, Side Effects).
  • Semantic Retrieval: Surfaces similar verified inquiries from the NIH MedQuAD reference repository.
  • Uncertainty Disclosure: Transparently highlights predictions with low confidence or high semantic entropy.

What the System NEVER Does

  • Never Diagnoses: Does NOT provide clinical diagnosis or tell a user what medical condition they have.
  • Never Prescribes: Does NOT prescribe medications, adjust drug doses, or recommend off-label pharmaceutical use.
  • Never Replaces Clinicians: Is NOT a substitute for face-to-face evaluation by board-certified healthcare professionals.
  • Never Generates Unverified Claims: Does not hallucinate medical facts; strictly uses grounded NIH reference data.
  • Never Misrepresents Certainty: Does not fabricate false confidence scores or overstate predictive certainty.

Responsible AI Engineering Principles

Patient-First Triage
Questions mentioning emergency keywords (e.g. crushing chest pain, slurred speech, anaphylaxis) trigger an immediate high-priority warning redirecting the user to emergency services.
Epistemic Humility
When a question is ambiguous or underspecified (such as single-word queries like 'diabetes?'), the model signals uncertainty and requests further clinical context rather than making overconfident assumptions.
Data Privacy by Design
Inquiries are processed locally without storing personally identifiable health information (PHI) or associating queries with user identities.

Known Limitations & Technical Disclosures

Dataset Representation: MedClass AI is trained on English-language clinical questions from the NIH MedQuAD corpus and curated open-domain inquiries. It is not currently optimized for non-English questions, non-standard medical vernacular, or pediatric slang.

Class Imbalance: While balanced sampling was implemented, conditions in ultra-rare diseases may exhibit higher predictive variance compared to common chronic conditions like diabetes or hypertension.

Clinical Verification: All predictions and routing suggestions are advisory and provided solely for clinical education, research exploration, and clinical inquiry routing.

Responsible AI & Clinical Disclaimer: MedClass AI is an NLP classification prototype developed for medical question intelligence and taxonomy mapping. It does NOT diagnose conditions, prescribe medications, or replace certified clinical judgment. If you are experiencing a medical emergency, immediately contact emergency services: 112 (National Emergency Helpline) or 108 (Ambulance).
